purpose: Separate reload-art handoff for the existing German rifleman; no runtime or accepted-atlas replacement.
referenceRecipe: First 128x128 cell of armies/game-ready/vojnici/nemacki-strelac-sprites.png, enlarged 4x using nearest neighbour.
prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve / existing game-sprite animation extension. Reference image 1 is the EXACT accepted soldier and firearm. Create EIGHT successive non-looping RELOAD frames for THIS SAME adult German soldier facing SCREEN RIGHT. Match his small light face, short olive field cap without new symbols, dark gray-olive uniform and trousers, tan paired belt pouches, black boots, thin dark pixel outlines and compact dark metal firearm with the existing bottom detachable magazine. Do not replace the gun with a long wooden rifle, do not give him a helmet, do not enlarge his face, do not upgrade the drawing into realistic art. This is a compact pixel-art character that will be displayed at about 80x80 pixels. Preserve the original equipment and proportions.
Layout: truly TRANSPARENT 1536x1024 canvas, EXACT FOUR columns by TWO rows; cells 384x512. Reading order left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Inside EACH cell the actual sprite rectangle is x=0..383, y=64..447, representing a 128x128 game frame at exactly 3x scale. Fixed ground at cell y=424, root x=192; at final 128px size the anchor is (64,120). Match reference silhouette: cap top around cell y=133 (23 game pixels below the sprite top), planted boots at y=424, body center near x=180, forward muzzle near x=321. Thus the whole character is only about 291px high within its cell, with wide TRANSPARENT margins. Keep the exact same unmoving legs, boots and pelvis in every frame; both feet remain planted. No body translation or changes of body scale. Only arms, firearm and very small head/shoulder movements animate. Do not paint a ground line, grid, backdrop, glow, shadow, text, numbers or captions. Do not draw bullets, muzzle flashes or smoke: this is reloading, NOT shooting.
Actions, eight frames: 1. EXACT reference horizontal READY/AIM stance, firing right hand on grip, left support hand forward on gun, stock at shoulder. 2. Lower weapon slightly off shoulder to chest-level handling position, muzzle still safely pointing right and slightly down. 3. Left support hand moves to grasp the bottom magazine; right firing hand remains on the same grip. 4. Left hand has pulled the OLD magazine clearly DOWN out of the gun, visible empty gap at the magazine well, then hand near belt pouch. 5. Left hand holds a NEW magazine just below the magazine well, visibly not seated yet. 6. Left hand pushes magazine UP fully into the well, clearly seated. 7. Keeping firing right hand on the grip, left hand reaches the side/top of the receiver and pulls the charging handle back; the gun remains pointed right, no long bolt-action rifle conversion. 8. Release/close the charging handle and return left hand to fore-end and stock to shoulder: clean original AIM pose again, fully ready, no flash.
Keep hand ownership and both arms anatomically consistent: no third arm, no duplicated magazines, no detached floating accessories. A hand-held old/new magazine is visible only during the relevant handling frames. Hard opaque sprite pixels and alpha-zero empty background only. Each of the eight poses must show the stated real hand/weapon action, not just whole-body breathing or recoloring.
weaponNote: Match the detachable bottom magazine visible in the accepted drawing; this package does not assert a historical firearm model.
selection: Eight poses with fixed boots. Low-alpha generated background removed during mechanical packing.
